title: Sinus surgery (FESS)
what: Working through the nostrils, the surgeon uses a thin camera and instruments to widen the sinus openings and clear what blocks them. There are no cuts on the face. It is usually done under general anesthesia.
why: For chronic sinusitis, nasal polyps, or sinus cysts, when medicines do not help.
duration: surgery usually takes 1 to 2 hours, with 1 to 3 days in hospital; if tissue was taken, lab results come in 1 to 2 weeks
tell_doctor: All your medicines, especially blood thinners. Your doctor will say what to stop and when
Any problems with anesthesia in you or relatives

prepare.title: Tests
prepare.text: You usually need a CT scan of the sinuses, blood tests, and an ECG. The clinic will give you a list.

prepare.title: Anesthetist
prepare.text: Before surgery, an anesthetist will talk with you. Tell them about your health and medicines.

prepare.title: Food
prepare.text: Usually no food from the night before and no drinks for a few hours. The clinic will tell you the exact time.

prepare.title: Things to pack
prepare.text: Comfortable clothes, tissues, a phone charger, and the medicines you take every day.

steps: On the day, you change, and an IV line is placed
In the operating room, the anesthetist gives anesthesia, and you fall asleep
The surgeon puts a thin camera and instruments into your nose
The sinus openings are widened, and polyps or cysts are removed
Sometimes soft packing or splints are placed in the nose
You wake up in the recovery room and are watched for a few hours
feel: Your nose is blocked, and you breathe through your mouth. This is expected in the first days
A dull ache or pressure in the face. You will get painkillers
A little bloody discharge from the nose in the first days
after: Any packing usually comes out after 1 to 2 days
Rinse your nose and have it cleaned at the clinic as scheduled. This matters for the result
For 1 to 2 weeks, do not blow your nose hard, lift heavy things, or bend suddenly
No saunas or hot baths until your doctor says it is OK
Breathing usually improves after a few weeks
red_flags: A nosebleed that does not stop in 10 to 15 minutes: call emergency services
A severe headache, vomiting, or a stiff neck: call emergency services
Swelling around the eye, double vision, or worse vision: see a doctor urgently or call emergency services
A fever over 38°C (100.4°F) and worsening pain

faq.q: Will there be scars on my face?
faq.a: No. The surgery is done through the nostrils, with no cuts outside.
Sometimes. To make it less likely, your doctor will prescribe treatment and regular checkups after surgery.

faq.q: When can I go back to work?
faq.a: Usually after 1 to 2 weeks, depending on your job. Your doctor will say.

reminders.text: Sinus surgery tomorrow. Pack your documents, CT scans, and medicine list. Eat and drink only until the time the clinic gave you.
